newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields defied weaker foreign markets on Wednesday and fell to record lows.

The impetus was taken from a Riksbank commissioned inflation survey pointing to overall lower inflation expectations and wage increases and a report by Swedish National Economic Research Institute KI forecasting lower inflation and higher growth.
A statement by S&P that the Swedish economy had improved solidely since 1995 also lent support, dealers said.
"The market has been in quite a bullish mood, especially for the shorter maturities ahead of the expected Riksbank corridor rate cut on Thursday," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates slid four basis points to 4.09 percent and the ten-year bond yields dropped three basis points to a record low 6.86 percent.
Meanwhile the spread between Swedish and German long yields decreased seven basis point to 120 points.
The crown was stable at 4.3465 against the mark compared to 4.3445 late on Tuesday.
